top.title: Anthropic's Claude Ship lets agents approve routine code changes under a plain-English policy
top.summary: Claude Ship adds agents that fix failing checks, resolve merge conflicts and respond to review feedback, plus Claude Approvals, which can merge routine changes on its own according to rules a team writes in plain English and stores in the repo. Approvals is in beta with an observe-only mode and spending limits, on Team and Enterprise plans.
top.why: The pattern (written approval policy kept next to the work, observe-only before enforcement) maps directly onto human-in-the-loop review for PMM workflows: define which outputs an agent may ship alone and which need a person.

top.title: Enterprises can now keep Claude prompts and responses in their own cloud
top.summary: Anthropic opened a public beta of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, which keeps Claude data in the customer's own cloud while still running Anthropic's automated misuse detection. It also relaxed retention rules for its top models so the required 30 days of prompts and responses can sit on customer servers.
top.why: This removes a common Legal/Security objection to sending marketing and customer data through Claude, so it belongs in your data-handling guardrail doc and in any IT intake conversation.

top.title: Google previews plain-language policies that check every agent action before it runs
top.summary: Google's semantic governance policies evaluate each action an agent proposes against rules written in ordinary language, such as never emailing earnings data to personal addresses, and can block it. A dry-run mode logs what would have been denied without stopping anything.
top.why: Pre-action policy checks are becoming a standard layer in agent platforms, which is both a guardrail design to borrow and a governance story Camunda's orchestration buyers will compare against.

try_this.title: Make the agent list approved assets before it drafts
try_this.how: Attach your approved messaging house, boilerplate and proof points to a drafting skill, and require it to first list which approved claims and blocks it will reuse and flag anything they can't cover, before writing a word. Review that list, then let it draft; compare the result against a run without the step.

workflows.title: Study: coding agents skip a company's approved components about 4 times in 10
workflows.summary: A vendor study of 15 large legacy codebases found two popular coding agents used the organization's own approved components only 55-59% of the time when given repo access but no rules, inventing or importing substitutes the rest. The vendor sells the fix, so treat the numbers as a warning, not a benchmark.
workflows.why: Access is not knowledge: the same drift happens when writing agents ignore approved messaging and templates, which argues for explicit reference files in every PMM skill.

workflows.title: A self-filling weekly marketing tracker in Google Sheets
workflows.summary: A reader built a scheduled weekly task that pulls numbers from analytics, ad and social tools into one Sheet, with screenshots covering the one source that isn't connected yet. It rolls up weekly, monthly, quarterly and yearly views automatically.
workflows.why: A simple template for a recurring PMM reporting workflow, including a pragmatic workaround for sources that lack a connector.

workflows.title: Canva's MCP server is now open to everyone
workflows.summary: Canva opened its design toolkit for AI agents to all users, so assistants that speak MCP can create and edit Canva designs.
workflows.why: Opens a path to connect drafting workflows straight to on-brand visual assets like one-pagers and social cards.

workflows.title: Two agent rules practitioners say actually help
workflows.summary: In a TLDR community thread, builders shared their most useful system-prompt rules: 'if an action can be undone, do it and tell me what you did' cut down routine questions, and 'revise only on new evidence or arguments' stopped Claude from flip-flopping under pushback.
workflows.why: Cheap additions to the standing instructions in your shared skills, worth testing for review-cycle workflows.

governance.title: Pennsylvania now requires AI-generated ads to carry a disclosure label
governance.summary: A new Pennsylvania law requires advertising made with AI to be labeled as such.
governance.why: State-level disclosure rules are arriving for marketing content, so your AI policy should say when a label is required and who checks.

competitive.title: Sierra raises $1.75B at a $30B valuation after passing $400M ARR
competitive.summary: Bret Taylor's customer-service agent company doubled its valuation in six months and says nearly half of the Fortune 50 are customers.
competitive.why: A strong signal that buyers will pay for domain-specific agents in production, which shapes how enterprises frame the build-vs-orchestrate question Camunda answers.

measurement.title: Chargebee's CEO on hybrid pricing for AI products and an open spec for agent costs
measurement.summary: Krish Subramanian argues usage-based pricing alone is not enough and that hybrid models with credits and subscriptions better reward repeat use. He also discusses AUDR, an open specification for tracking agent usage and costs, and why finance agents need citations, traceability and human review.
measurement.why: Useful input for AI pricing and packaging positioning, and AUDR is worth a look as a possible standard for reporting agent cost in your own adoption metrics.

measurement.title: Model updates now swing AI-search visibility the way algorithm updates swung SEO
measurement.summary: HubSpot data shows a ChatGPT update raised cited URLs per prompt 51%, a Gemini release cut citations 27% the same week, and Perplexity doubled citations while referral traffic fell 14%. Separate Semrush data shows UGC citations rising on Google's AI surfaces and falling on ChatGPT.
measurement.why: AI-visibility dashboards need release dates annotated, or model changes will be misread as content wins or losses.

measurement.title: AWS's Strands Decider v2 routes work between models to cut cost
measurement.summary: AWS released an open-weight model family that scores a list of options; AWS says routing between two Claude models with it solved 94% as many tasks at 44% of the cost.
measurement.why: Another data point that model routing is a real cost lever when you report on what AI workflows cost to run.

enablement.title: OpenAI pays local experts up to $8,000 a month to coach small businesses on AI
enablement.summary: OpenWorks, a pilot in 20 mostly Midwest and Southern US cities, pays tech-savvy locals to work hands-on with business owners on a problem the owner picks and to teach one community AI class a month. Participants get three free months of ChatGPT Business.
enablement.why: A paid, hands-on champion model (one real problem per person, plus a recurring class) is a useful reference design for an internal AI concierge program.

landscape.title: OpenAI puts a cheaper GPT-6.2 Sol into ChatGPT's default chat
landscape.summary: GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra launched across ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API, with OpenAI saying Sol lands within half a point of Astra at about one-fifth the cost at maximum reasoning effort; a chat-tuned Sol now handles the Chat tab.
landscape.why: Cheaper near-frontier models change the cost math for high-volume drafting steps in your workflows.

landscape.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after White House involvement
landscape.summary: Nvidia's board reversed itself and brought Huang back 11 days after he resigned, with President Trump saying he pushed for it; the stock added more than $1T in a day. Congressional hearings start Dec 1.
